pr_title: Cleanup after moving nordic counter drivers to use device tree
pr_body:
Cleanup after #55898.

Fixing compilation of `samples/drivers/counter/alarm` for nordic DKs.
Adding missing protection in `nrf_rtc_timer`.

Fixes #56105.
Fixes #56188.
pr_comments: @anangl can you take another look? I had to add one more commit.

issue_context.title: samples/drivers/counter/alarm fails for nrf boards in main branch
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
`samples/drivers/counter/alarm` fails to build for nrf52840dk_nrf52840, nrf51dk_nrf51422, nrf9160dk_nrf9160, nrf52dk_nrf52832

**To Reproduce**
Build the test for these boards.

**Expected behavior**
Twister build pass for these boards.

**Impact**
Blocking https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/56178

**Logs and console output**
See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/actions/runs/4510053473/jobs/7940581606?pr=56178

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA 2d26baaeb1b764350fe226a4089395d958154168

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments:
I am confused. COUNTER_NRF_RTC depends on rtc1, but here we enable rtc0, as well as in the board overlay files.
I don't understand why.

COUNTER_NRF_RTC is a flag that indicates that RTC based counter driver is used because there is at least one instance with that compatible enabled.
So if that implementation is enabled then we are taking `rtc0`.
It would probably be better to use a fixed label in all overlays and take that device.
Sorry, I mixed up NRF_RTC_TIMER and COUNTER_NRF_RTC  here.
